publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Firms in the high-tech sector establish strategic alliances (SAs) and are involved in merger and acquisition activities (M&As) to enhance their competitive position. The economic and managerial strands of literature about SAs and M&As tell us virtually nothing about the strategic choice of firms between based SAs and M&As. This article intends to fill this void by examining the circumstances in which firms have a preference for SAs or M&As as a mode for external technology sourcing. By focussing on the dyad as the unit of analysis, this study provides empirical support for the effect of prior direct and indirect ties on the current choice between SAs and M&As. Prior alliances between two companies increase the probability that one will acquire the other. On the contrary, indirect ties in the prior SA-network increase the probability that the two firms will form a SA. There are also relatively more M&As between firms from the same economic block (intra-triad). SAs are preferred between firms located in different economic blocks in the triad because of the higher risk they have to bear.

articleTitle: The patent portfolio for strategic R&D planning
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Empirical research shows a discrepancy between the perceived importance and the actual level of information on competitor's R&D strategies. It is argued that patent information might be used to overcome this information deficit. However, empirical research further reveals that patent information is rarely used in strategic R&D planning. The authors pick up this issue and introduce a patent portfolio, which, as it is known from various technology portfolios, helps companies to manage the effective allocation of scarce R&D resources. Based on patent data from six German and Japanese mechanical engineering companies, the authors show the application of patent portfolios for strategic R&D planning purposes. The patent portfolio proves to be a very valuable tool for R&D decision makers. Based on the experiences made in the case study, recommendations for the effective use of patent portfolios are formulated.

articleTitle: Entry into a global industry of proprietary technological systems-criticality of defense conversion and systems architecture
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Taiwan's government has officially targeted the commercial aircraft industry and the main force is a combat aircraft producer. However, the prospect of defense conversion is dismal because neither spin-off nor dual-use strategy can be applied effectively. Moreover, the integral architecture of the systems products constitutes an insurmountable barrier, leading to a prediction of the futility of this national move.

articleTitle: Public promotion of innovative engineering and technology
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Innovative technology based on scientific progress is recognized as an important factor in national economies. In times of slow growth and recessions, municipal, state legislatures and administrations are increasingly turning to engineering entrepreneurs and innovative businesses for renewed growth. Measures range from administrative and financial services to tax incentives and subsidies. The author describes a number of actual programs and discusses and evaluates the instruments used. The author discusses the expectations, national science progams, external factors, country programs (France, Great Britain, Germany, Japan, USA), education, basic research, large projects, technology procurement and transfer, and small industry.

articleTitle: Technics and systemicity: keys to technology management beyond year 2000
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Technique is characteristic of human organisation. As such, it has generated many significant works which vary in nature from the descriptive to the critical. Works by Gille, Ellul and Mumford should be recognised as part the epistomological base of technology management. A new systemic perspective on the technique outlined in this paper may provide keys to a new technology management paradigm for the new millennium.

articleTitle: New product introduction: reducing time to market using Internet and Intranet technology
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: The rate of technological advances over the past five to ten years has resulted in shortened product life cycles, making it necessary to engage in a continuous and rapid introduction of new products. The ability to anticipate and respond to market pressures makes the timely introduction of new products a crucial competency within many industries. While technological advances have driven the need for a reduced time to market, they also have provided tools to aid in the reduction of product development cycle time. This paper examines how the use of the Internet and Intranet in the new product introduction process can reduce time to market by facilitating increased levels of communication within a company and between a company and its customers, based on literature searches as well as interviews.

abstract: Start of the above-titled section of the conference proceedings record.

articleTitle: Technology transfer and sustainable development: the case of the Asean countries
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: This paper proposes an 'environmental friendly technology transfer model' (EFTTM) to facilitate the process of the transfer of environmental technology for the ASEAN countries. A survey was conducted to validate the proposed model in which four ASEAN countries participated. The result of the survey is discussed.

articleTitle: Processes of manufacturing and corporate strategy making: mutual influence and performance
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: The authors identify three processes of making corporate strategy and extend these to the processes of making manufacturing strategies; these are rationality, interaction and assertiveness. For different combinations of processes used for making corporate and manufacturing strategies, the authors give propositions to predict their effectiveness. They found substantial support for these propositions from the data on 24 leading manufacturing firms. Firms with "incremental" manufacturing strategies were less effective, and firms with "bold" manufacturing strategies which also emphasized the marketing function were most effective. Limited data revealed that to achieve effectiveness firms with "incremental" manufacturing strategies must also pursue "integrated" manufacturing strategies.

articleTitle: Intercultural negotiations for engineering projects: case study Vietnam
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Success in negotiations between East and West often hinges on cross-cultural issues. This paper presents a case study of negotiations between an Australian project team and the Vietnamese authorities to install the first mobile telecommunications network in the country. Issues during the design, development and delivery phase of the project are documented with particular reference to the use made of multimedia authoring facilities.

articleTitle: Concurrent engineering: an application in the hospitality industry
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. One of the trends in today's business environment is that of teams. One system for implementing teams is concurrent engineering. Several methodologies have been developed to utilize and manage concurrent engineering principles in the manufacturing industries. Process value estimation methodology (PVE) allows management to target processes that are ripe for reengineering and prevents cost reduction that decreases value. design for assembly (DFA), is another technique that increases the value of product by optimizing design through cost reduction focusing on the assembly process. Our study attempts to apply the PVE and DFA reengineering methodologies to the restaurant industry. We do this by exploring the product/process methods used in the restaurant industry and their relation to the product/process methods used in manufacturing. Questionnaires were distributed randomly to 150 Alien County restaurants and were to be answered by management respondents only. Although we rejected our hypothesis that the PVE and DFA methodologies are readily transferred to the service industry, it is clear that the reengineering techniques currently adhered to resemble some aspects of both methodologies. This discovery suggests that perhaps the service industry, or the restaurant industry, may want to define its own set of methodologies based on the unique criteria involved in redesigning or creating service-related processes/products.

articleTitle: Building competitive advantage through technology alliances
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. The high growth of strategic alliances and technology partnerships is fueled primarily by forces outside the control of corporate stewards: globalization, technological growth and socio-political factors. Continuous technological advancement is the objective and landmark of successful corporations. Limited corporate resources, escalating R&D costs and today's much larger pool of innovation sources make technology alliances a practical tool for attaining this objective. Relative to the past, more companies now look outside their R&D confines for their next technological breakthrough. Universities have been a party to a large extend in this development. Although university partnerships fall short of two important criteria for optimizing partnering success compatibility with business missions and long-term commitment-they are an important partner in helping industry to attain competitive advantage. The author proposes an alliance development model which has withstood the test of numerous such partnerships and alliances. Starting with the design of the right logic for a technology alliance to establishing partner selection criteria, this process follows a path thought to improve chances for success in this field, where failures exceed successes all too frequently. Guidelines for managing technology alliances-Golden Rules-are offered. The paper concludes with an optimistic outlook for technology alliances and similar partnerships between all types of enterprises.

articleTitle: Practices of technology monitoring and project evaluation in a sample of Brazilian companies
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. The opening up of Brazilian economy has brought drastic restructuring of local corporate strategies, and therefore subsequent modification of technology strategies. This study analyzes changes in the practices of technology monitoring and R&D project screening and evaluation through twelve companies. The results indicate that these companies are focusing on fewer products and are more attuned to their clients.

articleTitle: Integrative modeling of the technology management system
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. Technology decision making is modeled as taking place within a national (and increasingly global) general technology environment (GTE), which in turn is defined by six general environmental forces and two business/industry forces. Specific combinations of environmental forces together with business/industry forces define the specific technology environments of individual industries. The authors present a systems modeling approach which shows complex causal chains shaping technology opportunities and decisions, and system interfaces where government policy or managerial intervention could be effective.

articleTitle: Total productive maintenance and change over reduction engineering a way to increase quality and productivity
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. Total productive maintenance (TPM) and change over reduction engineering (CORE) are fundamental parts of the just-in-time production system and a way to increase productivity and quality. The major TPM improvement activities include maximizing equipment effectiveness, eliminating the six big equipment-related losses, autonomous maintenance by operators and small group activities, training to improve operation and maintenance skills and the promotion of maintainability from the design throughout the entire life span of the equipment. Set-up and adjustment is one of the six big losses of TPM, and single minute exchange of dies (SMED) is the heart of just-in-time production. CORE, using a newly developed software, takes SMED to a new dimension. With this approach, companies have typically achieved over 50 per cent change-over reduction. Some companies are achieving success with TPM: equipment downtimes are drastically reduced, equipment productivity is strongly increased, maintenance costs are reduced, process yields and product quality dramatically improved. This paper shows the fundamentals of TPM, its successful industrial application and some selected results of maintenance benchmarking in the manufacturing and process industry, which shows the present state and future development of equipment and maintenance management. The basics and some results of CORE are presented. Typically, the results are obtained in workshops in just a few days. CORE projects were carried out in several countries.

articleTitle: Employees' adaptation to technological changes in a multinational corporation in Malaysia
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: The present exploratory study examines the impact of technological changes on employee motivation and satisfaction. The results indicate that the ability to cope with technological changes, is linked to job specification. Higher level employees adapt better. A way of improving adaptation is to consult with all employees In the implementation of new technologies.

articleTitle: The evolution of machine tool technology in India-a principal components analysis
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. An understanding of the evolution of a technology, in terms of the changes in its characteristics, is essential for simulating improvements in the technology. This paper demonstrates the advantages of using principal components analysis to graphically study the evolution of the machine tool technology (specifically, turning machines) in India. Some policy implications are highlighted.

articleTitle: Study of American expatriate experiences in Taiwan
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. Past international human resource management literature has suggested that most American multinational firms that employ expatriate managers have difficulty successfully retaining these managers in overseas assignments. The purpose of this study is to examine the main reasons for the high failure rate of American expatriates in Taiwan and to seek proper methods to improve their chances of succeeding overseas. First, in order to delineate the current state of overseas relocation programs in US multinational corporations, the extensive literature was reviewed in the areas of expatriate failure rates, adjustment, selection criteria, preparation and training, long term management development strategies and repatriations. A questionnaire was administered on a group basis to 30 American expatriates who are currently working in Taiwan. Information gathered from those expatriates was used to examine their overall adjustment, with three different types of statistical analyses used to measure the results. Preparatory training for recently expatriated and lengths of time on current assignment were found to influence overall adjustment, while the marital status, previous international work experience, preparatory training, age, home countries (US, Europe and Canada) and cultural novelty had no relationship with the overall adjustment of American expatriates in Taiwan. Finally, the implication of the study's findings for American expatriates in Taiwan are discussed and recommendations for policy change are offered. Both research and practical implications of these findings are explored.

articleTitle: Critical knowledge areas: a linchpin between chaos and order
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. Discoveries made possible by advancing technology are giving researchers in a variety of sciences insight into many aspects of the world around us that have never before been accessible. A new realization of consistent patterns in how change, adaptation and evolution appear to occur has given rise to a new science called the science of complexity. One can use critical knowledge areas (CKAs), knowledge that is unique to the organization and gives it its competitive advantage, as a focal point as the concepts from this emerging field of thought are applied to technology-based organizations. In a technology environment, the success of the product that the firm is meant to generate depends on the ability to stay at the leading edge. The organization's most important assets for long term survivability lie in its CKAs and in the ability to acquire, retain and transfer knowledge and information. The set of CKA is the intellectual capital and intellectual capital demands continuous and purposeful investment.

articleTitle: Using the Austin Technology Incubator as an "innovation boot camp" and as a catalyst to foster global commercialization strategies
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. IC2 Institute, The University of Texas at Austin, launched the Austin Technology Incubator in 1989. Over the years, ATI has received several national awards and has been the model for technology commercialization centers within the US federal government and in other nations. ATI's "3M Innovation Boot Camp" is discussed as an innovative learning laboratory for large corporations.

articleTitle: A new R&D framework of telecommunications under competitive environment in Korea: the case of FPLMTS project
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. Korea has deployed a nationwide R&D framework to develop telecommunications technologies systematically. The main idea behind the framework was that government should lead the R&D program to strengthen national competitiveness. It was widely accepted that it was a very efficient R&D framework. The recent telecommunications environment, however, has been rapidly changed. Competition was introduced in the telecommunications service industry and its market has already been opened. With successful technology transfer from research institutes and investment by private firms in telecommunications technology, private firms have attained a level at which they can draw out all the potential of a new technology. With these changes, the traditional government-driven R&D framework is no longer fit to carry out R&D effectively. In this paper, a new telecommunications R&D framework has been described using the case of the FPLMTS project. It resembles the current R&D framework in that several parties collaborate. However, it is different from the current R&D framework in that each participating organization has its own research area as well as in that service providers can accumulate the acquired technologies. In this framework, government-owned telecommunication operators can participate fairly in R&D projects. There are still several issues to be resolved, however.

articleTitle: R&D institutes as focal points for innovation networks
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. The development of Chinese innovation system had long been focused on strengthening R&D institutes. The R&DIs thus played an important role in technology innovation in China. The policy measures for nurturing the growth of innovation networks have now mainly been concentrated on the linkage and cooperation between R&DIs and firms. More attention should be paid to the linkage and cooperation between innovative firms in innovative studies and innovation policy in China.

articleTitle: Business concepts analysis process
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: This paper defines a process for evaluating business process ideas and concepts. The emphasis is on the systematic analysis of the impact of anticipated change for business improvement and the potential cost and benefits to the business process using quality function deployment techniques. The process is applicable to the process management or process engineering of large-scale business processes spanning across multiple organizations. The process may be too expensive to apply to detailed work group level processes; however it is very much needed in order to manage business processes across large corporations, across divisions or for other large organizations.

articleTitle: Impact of electronic integration on new product development between firms
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. This project examines the use of electronic integration between two firms engaged in co-developing a new product. The authors are interested in uncovering the process by which the two companies moved towards a common information network and new product development process, given their diversity in organizational structure and culture.

articleTitle: Dynamics of firm-level technological capabilities in an LDC-a conceptual model
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Specific studies are needed on firm-level technological capabilities (FTC) in less-developed countries (LDCs). Unlike macro-level issues related to FTC, which have received considerable research attention, micro-level issues are yet to receive the attention they deserve. This paper proposes a micro-level conceptual model for understanding the dynamics of FTC in the Indian capital goods sector. The model leads to several hypotheses about the nature of inter-relationships between FTC and the relevant firm-level factors.

articleTitle: Teaching management skills to engineering undergraduates-the Trinity experience
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. Civil engineering has been taught in Trinity College Dublin since 1842. From the outset the emphasis has always been on providing a broad well-rounded education. Increasingly, attention is given to the teaching of management and communication skills. These skills are important for technology management. This paper describes 'The Engineer, Management and Society' programme which is obligatory for all engineering students during the last two years of the four year undergraduate course. Included are elements of law, economics, management, business skills, economics and communication skills. The paper outlines some of the advantages and disadvantages of the present approach to teaching these subjects. The communication skills module is described as an example, referring to the relevance of modern electronic communications in the engineering profession as well as the traditional skills of report writing and oral presentations. The paper explains how some of the objectives of the course are met by coursework, projects and other aspects of the degree programme, and also mentions some of the other aspects of the undergraduate course relevant to technology management. Conclusions are presented on the Trinity experience of teaching management skills to engineering students, with suggestions on possible future developments.

articleTitle: Benchmarking patenting procedures: a conceptual model of the procedure and experiences of R&D scientists
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. When economic policies liberalize the competitive efficiency of the National Patent System (NPS) is of immense significance. The stress on global leadership through technological breakthrough brings in the agenda for protection. With the 1991 economic liberalization, India is witnessing this paradigm shift. Steps towards building a patent culture is visible in science and technology laboratories such as the CSIR and IISc. The need to understand what other nations are doing and benchmark the patent process is imperative for the competitive efficiency of the NPS. The stages that R&D personnel go through are eight in number. They are idea, R&D activity, writing the technical specification, Patent Office (PO) evaluation, clarifications, award of patent, the reward for patent and commercialization and publications. At each of these phases, various components that are crucial in a NPS play a role. The components such as PO, organizational factors, legal infrastructure, scientist and informational databases are illustrated in the paper. The processes and procedures of these components can be measured for efficiency. A framework of component processes for each stage developed based on the Indian procedures can be compared for efficiency across nations and benchmarked. This will provide an international standard of efficiency of the NPS. It will provide for more progressive and competitive patent worthy R&D.

articleTitle: Recent development in engineering management education in Australia, Britain and USA
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. This paper examines some major recent developments in engineering management education in Australia, New Zealand, Britain and the USA. Some comparisons and contrasts are made. Australia has a unique arrangement in that the Institution of Engineers, stipulates a mandatory condition that 10 percent of all engineering undergraduate courses must be in engineering management. New Zealand and British engineering courses introduce EM studies in undergraduate programs. The USA has the largest and most advanced EM programs, with Australia increasing its graduate EM programs. Britain relies more on a Graduate Diploma program in EM administered by its council of engineering institutions, but Australia is more likely to follow the USA in graduate programs.

articleTitle: Analysis of affecting factors in business process reengineering in Chinese automotive industry
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper begins with looking at the content and context of business process reengineering (BPR). We examine the situation and development stage of the Chinese automotive industry. Three major advancements are discussed: the application of computers developed from production management to synthesized information systems; CAD/CAM techniques were applied to envigorate the development of new vehicles; and old equipment was improved by using IT. But the Chinese automotive industry is still at the primary stage of automation and facing many crises. We identify the most outstanding affecting factors of BPR of the Chinese automotive industry as follows: the restraint of traditional mode of thinking; inferior quality of personnel; and the form of organization is out-of-date. The hierarchy, over staffed, power concentrated function management is not designed to focus on process. It carries historical inertia and will deter the BPR. As our conclusion, we hold that BPR is an integrating process of "hardware" (equipment) and "software" (made of thinking, quality of personnel and organization structure). The construction of "software" consumes much cost and time. Therefore, we suggest that the first step in carrying out BPR should be the transformation of these "software" affecting factors.

articleTitle: Innovational output and its pricing strategy in the firm level
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. To secure the advantage from innovation each firm competitively invests on the R&D program. Moreover price competition take place simultaneously with R&D competition in the market. Accordingly in order to make the success of their R&D to be realized, marketing aspects of innovational output should be considered in the initial stage of R&D. This paper proposes pricing strategy of innovating firms when they have a successful R&D. Interdependent and independent R&D schemes are organized to tackle this problem. In the presence of spillover innovating firms face a tradeoff between incentives to undertake R&D and the costless benefits from rival competitor's innovation. Interdependent R&D can be interpreted as an attempt to internalization of the externality which takes place in that context. The model focuses on pricing of innovational output. This make a difference from other literatures on R&D with spillovers. Defining the spillover and output-sharing rules, a basic model of analysis is developed and demonstrates the analysis on pricing decision for two types of R&D behavior-interdependent and independent R&D.

articleTitle: Industrial project selection criteria in the Sultanate of Oman
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. This paper examines the criteria of industrial project selection decision-making in the Sultanate of Oman. Twenty-five basic criteria are used to evaluate each project with respect to its impact on them. These criteria are grouped into five categories namely; financial, marketing, technical, economic and strategic criteria. Each criterion has been defined by experts from Ministry of Commerce and Industry in the Sultanate of Oman.

articleTitle: Core technological competence and growth strategies of corporations
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. The ability of a manufacturing enterprise to gain competitive advantage is a function of its technological core competence. This paper examines the process used by large corporations to build technological competence by establishing "a multitude of new co-productive relationships in the form of alliances, joint ventures, outsourced subcontracting, etc." A resource based view of technological competence is developed. The problems of integrating discrete technological competence are studied in the context of the acquisition of NCR by AT&T and Lotus Development Corporation by IBM.

articleTitle: OCCAM: a collective procedure supporting analysis and management of new technologies
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given a follows. New technologies, mainly computer based technologies oriented to a multiplicity of functions, require special attention both in development and insertion processes. The adoption of a conceptual framework from literature, and its operationalization, by means of a system of structured schemes in a procedure of collective analysis and management, may supply appropriate "tools" for supporting new technology development, validation and controlled insertion in organization. The integrated use of schemes and different techniques in a collective process of analysis, planning and control is described in this paper. The main schemes are presented in detail, together with some results that have arisen from the applications of the system.

articleTitle: Modified process control chart in IC fabrication using clustering analysis
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. During the complicated production process in integrated circuit (IC) fabrication, various types of defects on wafer surface are unavoidable. As the wafer size increases, the clustering phenomenon of the defects becomes increasingly apparent. To upgrade the yield and reliability of IC products, statistical process control (SPC) is practiced to track a manufacturing process. However, the clustered defects frequently cause many false alarms when the standard control charts for defects is used. In this study, we propose a method for constructing defect control charts for processes that yield clustered defects. A case study is also evaluated, indicating that the proposed method produces satisfactory control charts for the defect data in IC fabrication.

articleTitle: Are ethical considerations culture specific in international technology transfer?
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. One of the great debates in ethics has always been to decide if there is one great master plan for ethical behavior that is universally acceptable. The problem with this debate is that there are dozens of different models of what ethical behavior should be. This paper is the result of research, interviews and case studies with a variety of different nationalities. It expresses and compares the differing points of view on the cultural-ethical conflicts of technology transfer.

articleTitle: Transferring knowledge within the company in the R&D arena
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. In the research and development (R&D) arena, the ability to transfer knowledge quickly and efficiently among groups within the company has become increasingly critical. This capability is at the heart of how organizations learn, adapt and innovate, and it is especially crucial in R&D, one of the most learning-intensive environments in the modern corporation. The author present recent research in this area, which draws upon literature, field interviews, and an on-going academia/industry dialogue, and suggests that this critical knowledge transfer is especially crucial at a small number of key crossroads in the management of technology.

articleTitle: How to overcome the "low level pitfall" in Chinese high-technology industry development: systematic view on the R&D activities and its investment
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. Chinese high-technology industries have to face the difficulties of relatively low capital accumulation, low R&D competence and imperfect institution infrastructure, etc. How to help them to enter into good evolutionary processes by technological and institutional innovation is really an important and challenging problem to the theory and practice of technology management in developing countries. In this paper, the authors analyze the problem from the point of systems evolutionary dynamics and try to present some policy suggestions.

articleTitle: Environmental wind-tunnel testing throughput [automobile R&D]
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. US automobile manufacturers must decrease time to market. Testing is a key element of the development process. A team of engineering managers applied theory of constraints, simulation modeling and theory of inventive problem solving, to develop measures of performance, strategies and inventions for increasing throughput in the wind tunnel.

articleTitle: Competitiveness and TQM: is the synergy really a surprise?
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. Media reports about today's successful enterprises increasingly scoop out one key factor-the proximity of these companies' management practices to total quality management (TQM), a distinct socially transmitted pattern of behaviour. This paper examines what makes TQM so different, its dividends, and why a company-wide obsession focused on satisfying customers, internal and external, leads a company to a stronger competitive position. Four essentials characterize TQM, as follows: top management's direct involvement in the delivery of quality; an uncompromising customer orientation; company-wide participation in the attainment of customer satisfaction; and the use of systematic methods used in resolving quality problems. TQM requires nonstop effort to eliminate tasks and processes that are nonvalue adding as far as the customer is concerned. Such savings are the "bottomline" benefits of TQM that the business can enjoy-even if there is no competition. But then, if whatever we produce must satisfy the internal and external customers and we produce nothing else, then we produce no waste, rework or redress. Then we do not have to raise prices to recover the cost of such waste from the customer, the goodwill we build here being the added edge in the marketplace. This strengthens the company's competitive stance, underscoring the synergy between TQM and competitiveness.

articleTitle: An intelligent constrained network approach in product development
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. This paper describes a framework for using intelligent constrained network approach in product development. An illustrative case study is presented to demonstrate the concepts.

articleTitle: Mining organizational culture: critical knowledge areas and breakthrough concepts
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Exponential growth in technology and emerging organizational prototypes signal the advent of cultural evolution. Leadership must now develop radically new adaptive strategies for survival. Our ancestors survived by successfully using undeveloped critical knowledge areas (CKAs) generating a technology-based cultural shift 10000 years ago. Today, leadership must mine organizational cultures for new CKA and breakthrough concepts. The author presents anthropological insights about culture, CKA and qualitative methodologies for assessing complex organizational systems.

articleTitle: Engineering management curricula of some tertiary institutions in Southern Africa
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. Engineering management curricula of some tertiary institutions in Southern African countries were studied considering the depth of coverage, time status of the various techniques dealt with and relevance to today's economic and technological demands. These parameters were compared with those of other tertiary institutions in certain developed countries such as the United States of America and Japan.

articleTitle: Managing competence development in production chains
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. In much of today's technology management, there seems to be a paradox between developing competencies and outsourcing. This leads to consideration of how firms can manage and improve the development of their competencies, when the competence are distributed throughout the firm's production chain. In this paper, it is argued that this represents a special problem in relation to competence development, mainly due to the fact that, in a production chain, firms are legally and organizationally separate entities. Furthermore, it is argued that competence development and organization for learning are possible means for developing competencies in production chains.

articleTitle: Models for successful education programs
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. Most organizations endure years of struggles, trying to fulfil imaginary expectations of their membership on educational issues. IEEE EMS is no exception. Many surveys have been collected over the years, with varying implementations of survey data. This paper looks into two unusually successful programs from the Mid-Atlantic region of the USA. The Washington DC, Section of the IEEE has conducted successful seminars over the years, primarily in the areas of emerging technologies and self-growth, such as Starting and Financing Your Own Business. In contrast, the Washington DC Chapter of the Association of Computing Machinery has sponsored a series of ten, one-day professional development seminars devoted to topics in data processing and computer science.

articleTitle: Competitive strategic elements and their roles in manufacturing planning
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: This paper studies and identifies seven competitive strategic elements (price, product differentiation, quality image, quality of performance, flexibility and service after delivery) and their relative importance in forming strategic plans. The conjoint analysis has been used to identify how consumers form their preferences in regard to the aforementioned elements. The results suggest a new direction for forming consumer-driven strategic plans.

articleTitle: Advance technology or local inexpensive industries, policy options for development
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. Industrial and technological growth in under-developed countries may not be feasible without the production of quality products and at a suitable price. The word "product" is used in its general context which includes material goods, services and know how. Thus, production of goods and services with quality standards and at a suitable price, is considered here as the principle goal of economic development plans in developing countries. The experiences gained from some of the advanced countries indicate that the realization of economic development plans, is only possible by a steady utilization of modern technologies and not the inefficient means of production and services which exists now in most of the developing countries.

articleTitle: Waste not, want not?: the relationship between manufacturers' adoption of innovative workplace management and pollution prevention practices
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: This paper presents an empirical analysis of the relationships between a manufacturing facilities' adoption of innovative pollution prevention techniques (i.e., source reduction and recycling) and of innovative workplace management practices (e.g., TQM, R&D, worker teams, etc.). It specifically evaluates whether facilities that are innovative in their manufacturing are also innovative in environmental practices.

articleTitle: Decision making in management of scientific projects
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. The paper considers the set of organizational mechanisms, which are used in the design and in the management of scientific projects. The proposed set of organizational mechanisms includes: expert and multi-criteria estimation, incentive mechanisms, resource allocation mechanisms, risk management procedures, etc. Particular attention is devoted to the consideration of project participant's activity-their ability for purposeful behavior in accordance with their interests.

articleTitle: An expert system for international patent advice
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. The recent creation of the World Trade Organization (Geneva) and the proposed expansion of the European Patent System into Eastern Europe will require RD&E managers, engineers and scientists to think about patents and intellectual property protection in new ways. This paper reports on the results of a Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Phase I effort to design an expert system to advise middle school, high school and undergraduate science and engineering students in the procedures and steps necessary to file US and International Patent Applications.

articleTitle: Benchmarking as a tool to facilitate the implementation of new technology
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. Structured benchmarking is a relatively new addition to the plethora of organizational improvement tools. The idea is simple and attractive. In general term, benchmarking enables learning, adapting, and implementing best practices of the leading companies. It is an attempt to encourage organizations to move away from the syndrome of "not invented here" towards learning from one another. Benchmarking is often used for improvement of existing processes, but rarely as a tool for planning the implementation of new technology.

articleTitle: A system for one of your most important plant assets-instrument information
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. An Instrument Information Management System provides an organized environment to efficiently manage, save and retrieve instrument related data and then maintain all of the current application, specification, and configuration information of an instrument in a cost effective manner throughout its life cycle.

articleTitle: Managing prototype reduction with mathematical programming
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. This paper describes a math programming model used to construct a minimal shared prototype fleet that meets all testing needs. The model is run iteratively to guide a test plan development process that involves ongoing dialogue between test requesters and fleet planners. We also discuss a host of implementation issues.

articleTitle: US high-technology export controls in a changed global environment, firm size, and competitiveness
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. With policies that impose barriers to export sales that do not exist for domestic sales, exporting of high technology products with actual or potential military applications have faced different treatment in the United States, for national security reasons. This paper explored the direct and indirect implications of high-technology export controls for the high-technology industry, by firm size and the overall US economy, using a fully specified recursive regression model on time series data for a 15 year period. An indirect effect is observed-whereby the export performance of particularly small high technology firms which appears to contribute positively to US global competitiveness, is adversely affected by export controls. Intuitively, small firms may depend more on direct export sales than the big firms which have other means (foreign direct investment, the use of overseas affiliates for foreign sales, etc.) of reaching international markets.

articleTitle: Characteristics of technologies and their meaning for new technology-based firms (NTBF)
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Based on the assessment by 81 experts of a two-round Delphi Survey conducted in 1996, the article compares such characterstics of technological areas as new materials, optics, software, and biotechnology. The investigation focuses on innovation in NTBFs. Confronting the results with the potential of start-ups advice for technology policies and consulting are derived.

articleTitle: Management of R&D projects for best quality and minimal risk
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. The new product development process is a specific example of an R&D project. Rapid product development methods, based on concurrent engineering, increase the risk of project and product failure or its substandard quality. A research survey conducted among professionals involved in product development activity confirms that unrecognized or ignored risk and indecisiveness are responsible for a majority of project and product failures, which happen to 46% of new products on the market. The authors propose a new approach to project management based on risk assessment and decision making techniques.

articleTitle: Using a new patent based technology indicator to measure the pace of technological progress for superconductor and semiconductor technologies
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: This study used the technology cycle time indicator (TCT) to measure the pace of technological progress in superconductor and semiconductor technologies, then to demonstrate its validity, compared it with the real cycles of technological progress described by the technology experts. The study also used the TCT to assess the positions of various countries patenting in the semiconductor technology field, then checked how the TCT assessment corresponded with the experts' assessments. The findings revealed that the TCT provided good assessment in each situation.

articleTitle: Managing tradeoff in product design decisions
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. This paper describes a structured trade-off approach that was used to make a series of product design decisions. The decision scope ranged from those that required broad stakeholder involvement to decisions that could be made by an individual engineer. The methodology allows for the assessment of risk and facilitates updating the intuition of all stakeholders.

articleTitle: Taguchi technique in controlling the moisture in cigarette manufacturing
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary for only given as follows. This study is made in a cigarette manufacturing unit to control the moisture variation and attain a target value. During the process steam is passed and drying also takes place due to several reasons. The final product has to maintain a target value. To attain this moisture level, in between the process also has to be maintained at a specific target. There are three grades of tobacco in the production line with given weightages to obtain the quality of the specified cigarette brand. As preliminary study a crucial stage in the process is selected to control the moisture variation. Six control factors and their levels are found out by brainstorming method. Since this is a case of attaining the average target value with "nominal is the best" and reduction in variation, the appropriate S/N value is chosen. Three control factors are found to be significant in the ANOVA of S/N ratio. Giving proper weightages to the three grades the levels of the maximum S/N ratios are chosen. ANOVA with the control factors are done and the significant factors are found out. The average values of the parameters which are close to the target value are chosen. For the fine tuning the parameter values were interpolated with polynomial decomposition. A linear fit was found to be appropriate. A compromise of the levels of the parameters is arrived at with due consideration for the weightages of the input grades. Since one of the parameters is easy to change during the process, separate levels were found out for three grades. The confirmation test resulted with substantial reduction in the variation and with attaining the moisture level very close to the target value.

articleTitle: A study on the QCC training practice in Taiwan
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary for only given as follows. QCC is the key to meet the needs of productivity improvement, yet there are some educational problems to facilitate the implementation of QCC in manufacturing which the study attempts to investigate: (1) the problem factors for the QCC workers who take the training courses of QCC, (2) applying the methods of the training to the QCC tools, and (3) the main problems for not using the methods during working. 3040 QCC workers' opinions were collected and analyzed. Some conclusions and suggestions were drawn to improve the QC training practice.

articleTitle: Applying systems engineering to the organization: announcing the Excellence paradigm
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: This paper introduces the "Excellence paradigm" a paradigm for an information age organization. It was developed by applying systems engineering to an organization and using technology to replace managers. The paper presents a brief overview of the Excellence paradigm, how command and control is achieved, and how work is done.

articleTitle: Updating engineering programs in Third World Countries: a successful strategy
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. Today's fast technological growth demands that engineering schools often update their programs and facilities. However, in Third World Countries, more specifically, in Latin American Countries, most universities are solely supported by governmental funds and are unable to keep up with the fast technological growth rate at this turn of the century. The engineering school at UFF in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, has launched a strategy towards both overcoming financial problems and keeping up with modernization. This paper is a case study of that strategy, and it may be useful for other engineering schools in Latin America.

articleTitle: Policy issues for technology transfer in developing countries, an analysis of alternatives
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. In this paper some of the policy issues in the transfer of technology to developing countries are examined. Technology transfer is considered within the context of production function by which the role of a given technology transfer policy in promoting the production of goods and services is discussed. It is argued that several factors influence the effective implementation of a given policy option. These include: (a) availability of materials may be are referred to as the hardware; (b) technical know-how and skilled work forces referred to as the software; and (c) the necessary organization in the which integration of capital and a skilled work force can take place. Other factors such as government policies and socio-cultural attitude towards learning and work habits of the recipient country may also significantly influence the implementation of a given technology transfer plan. As such, no single policy option can be considered to be an optimum policy to be applied in all of the developing countries.

articleTitle: Profit Impact from Change Strategy in the Swedish automotive value-chain
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. In a comprehensive bench-marking panel-study, the Swedish automotive industry is analyzed and described in terms of how current change activities influence manufacturing and business performance. Over 100 manufacturers along the value chain, from manufacturers of raw materials to the car manufacturers assembly units participate in this panel-study called PICS-Profit Impact from Change Strategy.

articleTitle: The product is dead!
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: To make better use of time within a product cycle, producers of high tech products begin marketing prior to the full specification of the product. Now, they may no longer finalize the physical specification at all. We can thus proclaim, "The product is dead." We present evidence for and implications of the death of the high tech tangible product.

articleTitle: Scaling issues in IS staffing-a city government example
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. Traditional IS organizational structures cannot simultaneously support the growth of networks and demands for other new technologies, while decreasing costs. This paper examines the transition to a more flexible structure that can be scaled to meet these new demands-using the Municipality of Anchorage as a case study.

articleTitle: Technology development chain's broken and recovered
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. This paper advances a new viewpoint about the technology development chain. It suggests that effective technology development is a continuous cycle chain. The author suggests "the method, of time series division" personally. By this method, three types of breakage phenomena in the chain are analyzed in detail. The paper also advances strategies for restoring the breakage points in the chain. This paper analyzes how technology development succeeds.

articleTitle: A process-variable model of the implementation of advanced manufacturing technology
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. This paper proposes a new conceptual approach in investigating the implementation of advanced manufacturing technology (AMT). This approach considers underlying implementation processes to provide theoretical explanations for hypothesized relationships between organizational variables such as culture and success in AMT implementation.

articleTitle: Globalization of technology and polycultural global teams
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. All firms, and in particular technology-driven organizations in the USA, are earning increasingly more revenues in global markets. Their technology value adding chains extend beyond their national boundaries and cultural space. This requires people with multiple cultures working together harmoniously. This paper discusses these international issues with requirements for high performing teams.

articleTitle: Quantitative methods for the economic appraisal of a new technology: a critical review
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. In the light of considerations of quantitative methods for the analysis of technological innovation, the paper presents a critical review of the most prominent evaluation techniques aiming to assess their strengths and weaknesses when applied in the appraisal of new technologies. The result of the study is summarized in two tables. In the first, the surveyed techniques are compared along seven dimensions that outline the resource and data needs; the constraints that influence the resulting outcomes; how risk and uncertainty are dealt; the main advantages and weaknesses; and the kind of problem that are best fitted by a given method. In the second, the operational usefulness (a mix of ease of use, transparency and unambiguousness) of the various methods is evaluated. In conclusion, the study underlines that: (a) the efficacy of each method does not univocally stand on its analytical sophistication, but rather on how the nature of decision the problem fits the theoretical and practical features of the evaluation technique; and (b) the recent tendency towards a combining use of different approaches seems to be a promising way to overcome the pitfalls of the single method.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis for R&D organizational process between US and Japanese companies: a case study of VCR manufacturers
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. The innovation process of video cassette recorders (VCRs) for home use was analyzed using patents applications and academic papers and partly added facts by interviews for Ampex, RCA, JVC and Sony. R&D organizational processes were analyzed comparatively among the companies studied.

articleTitle: Technology evolution of ATM and copier machine: analyses based on commercially available data
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. A main problem in studies of technology evolution is the difficulty in obtaining reliable data in a cost-effective way. This study uses commercially available data to analyze the evolution of ATM and copier machines in the last 20 years. In this way, the authors are able to observe the emergence of dominant designs and to draw relevance trees. Problems with these data sources are discussed.

articleTitle: Evaluating team performance in a maturity model framework
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: This paper discusses the issue of team responsibilities and performance evaluation in software development environments that have adopted the capability maturity model as a process improvement model. The team performance criteria discussed in this paper provide a basis for an evaluation and reward system that reinforces the principles of a process-focused environment.

articleTitle: An information model for quality improvement programs
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. We propose a model for handling quality information with the aim of improving quality and productivity in an organization. A hierarchical model of information is based on three levels: control of the process; evaluation of the process; organizational assessment. The three levels are described and a field application is presented and discussed. The approach from which the model was developed stems from an interdisciplinary combination of industrial engineering, information systems, organizational psychology and industrial statistics. The proposed model, in our field-tested experience, improves the chances for a successful realization of the improvement potential in the organization.

articleTitle: Product data modeling and business
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. This paper considers the development of product data modeling and its implementation in the business enterprise. PDM is only one of many technologies that have been developed to assist in the management of engineering information and although some success has been achieved many organizations are having difficulties in obtaining the maximum benefit. This may be due to our lack of understanding of the problem or the crudeness of the technologies, but it is suggested that this may be remedied by considering the place of the technology in the whole of the enterprise information system and developing an enterprise wide information strategy. Two case studies are used for illustration and proposals for further research made.

articleTitle: Economic analysis and synthesis of technology investment strategies in manufacturing
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Analyzing and justifying an investment strategy that changes the production system from continuous manufacturing to small batch flexible manufacturing while maintaining competitive characteristics such as cost is a significant undertaking. Considerable discussion in the literature has produced a number of useful concepts and alternative models for examining manufacturing system investments. The most difficult problems to overcome; however, remain those that involve estimating the actual costs and benefits that will accrue as a result of an investment. The problem of financially analyzing the investment hasn't changed. This paper presents the development of an enterprise decision support model (EDSM) used to analyze investment decisions for system performance and to determine the most beneficial sequence for deploying a group of investments. The approach uses discrete event simulation to create the EDSM and capital budgeting techniques to develop a cumulative net present value (CNPV) function for competing investment implementation choices. EDSMs support the evaluation procedure by making a comprehensive system model a formal part of the strategic planning and decision process. The approach was investigated using a local manufacturing company as a test case. The results of the investigation are provided as well as a discussion regarding this approach to decision analysis.

articleTitle: Organizational mythology
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. Although most people think of "myths" as untruths (or, at best, based on faulty logic), as in "that's only a myth", in fact, in the true anthropological sense, myths are simply "cultural stories or lessons" (which, ultimately, may or may not be true). More precisely, an organization uses its mythology to socialize its members such that they understand, or interpret, their experiences in a way which is supportive of the organization's overall goals. Myths exist at all levels-from global myths to ones held individually. Consider, for an example of a "national" myth, that, in the settling of the West in the 1800s, citizens were encouraged to settle semi-arid Western lands based on a myth-"rain follows the plow". Settlers believed this religious-based myth and made life decisions based on it. Or consider a well known business organization myth-"what's good for General Motors is good for America". "Organizational myths" are defined as unwritten, orally communicated but often unspoken beliefs that control organizations. It is contended that underlying all aspects of an organization are the totality of its beliefs and values, as manifested in its myths. Studies have documented that organizations, particularly technology-based ones, deal poorly with the "soft" (people) side of their business, i.e., the intangibles of which an organization's beliefs, as manifest in its myths, are paramount. Methodologies to identify and analyze an organization's myths have been developed and are described.

articleTitle: An apprentice design/decision approach
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper attempts to show the importance, the simplicity and the complexity of managing interactions between design support environment users and their information systems. It presents the problematic approach on human system learning in an integrated design environment by suggesting a very interactive apprentice system approach.

articleTitle: Organisational support in managing transition of engineers into management roles-an empirical study in Australia
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Though a significant number of engineers move into management roles in their careers, a majority of these transitions are viewed as unsuccessful. This paper, based on a survey of engineers in Australia, concludes that the responsibility for managing and coping with these transitions are primarily left to the individuals, with negligible support and resources provided by the organisations in Australia.

articleTitle: Creating a useful mission planning system for the F15-E of 2000
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. The USAF F-15E community relies on a problem-plagued workstation network for mission planning. This paper describes the effort to develop and deploy a PC based system for a typical F-15E squadron. The system and lessons learned are the basis for recommendations on mission planning systems within the USAF.

articleTitle: A multi-organizational "skunk works" for product design in a small business
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: This paper has presented a case study of the commercial design management of an instrumentation system to detect fallen power lines on electric distribution systems. The design was performed in an ad hoc "skunk works" consisting of individuals from several different organizations brought to a small business organization for the sole purpose of accomplishing the project on an aggressive schedule. The project successfully met its objectives of schedule cost and product requirements, and serves as an excellent study of new product design in an innovative environment.

articleTitle: Accurate evaluation and improvement for operational efficiency of transportation systems
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. In general, mineral transport systems include mineral conveying and truck transport subsystems. The paper presents a combination of simulation, network and optimization models to develop a decision support system for mineral transportation decisions. It applies data envelopment analysis (DEA) methods and models to evaluate and improve the operational efficiency of such transportation systems. The simulation model has the advantage of random data processing that is very suitable for mineral conveying systems. The paper applies simulation and network models to describe the mineral transport process. DEA is an approach to measuring the efficiency of entities. The new DEA model can also optimize inefficient entities. DEA has several properties which make it attractive as a tool for evaluating and improving the operational efficiency of transportation systems effectively. The simulation model and optimization model, which are based on DEA, cooperate with each other, and provide a powerful function to help managers in decision making.

articleTitle: Selection and implementation of information technology in the health care industry
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: A telephone survey was conducted with office representatives of 407 physician practices in Oregon. The purpose was to determine the selection and implementation processes related to software decisions. The respondents also rated the impacts of the software on the practice. The results are examined relative to practice size and type, cost of software, prior software experience and type of software.

articleTitle: Towards integrating software technology and competitive strategies
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Process maturity models are used not only to assess the capability of software development organization but also as a tool to identify areas that need improvement. These models, however, may not be applicable to all organizations in equal degree and they are not connected with business objectives. This paper presents a framework that integrates the strategic planning process with software process improvement planning. Through an iterative approach, competitive and technology strategies are identified and the process improvement plan can be defined according to these strategies.

articleTitle: Key success factors affecting choice in an emergent technology base
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given as follows. Micro-electro-mechanical-systems are projected to comprise a $15 billion market in the year 2000. Pacific Rim companies will produce 30% of these new products. Preliminary findings of a major field study report on issues including core competencies, and choice of technology base from a field of up to seven competing technologies.

articleTitle: Results from process assessments in software companies
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: The capability maturity model was originally developed for large military and aerospace contractors. It represents an excellent framework of software process concepts and embodies some general principles which apply to companies of any size and product orientation. We found, however, that it was less suited for small and medium sized enterprises. This paper describes three years of experience with a modified assessment technique. The paper also looks beyond process related issues and analyzes other fundamental problems which are rooted in the management of software.

articleTitle: Necessary conditions for successful company research
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Industrial research can serve many functions. If applied continuously, these functions help to build research potentials. We identify five potentials: an identification potential, an external knowledge transfer potential, a creative or inventive potential, and an internal research result transfer potential. Assuming that either one of these potentials is present or is missing, we find 16 different situations of a research laboratory. We make plausible that in most of these situations the necessary conditions for research to contribute successfully to the competitiveness of the firm are not met. Considering one example, we discuss how weaknesses of a potential can be identified, and what could be done to build a missing potential.

articleTitle: Structural options for Turkish construction companies' organizational design
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only given. In recent years, top-level managers in many of today's leading corporations are losing control of their companies. The problem is not that they have misjudged the demands created by an increasingly complex environment and an accelerating rate of environmental change, nor even that they have failed to develop strategies appropriate to the new challenges. The problem is that their companies are organizationally incapable of carrying out the sophisticated strategies they have developed. Here, structural options for the organizational design of construction companies in Turkey are described by the author.

articleTitle: Simulation based approach to modeling product and process interactions
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. The major corporate goals of any enterprise are to make more profit, increase its market share and provide workforce stability among others. To achieve these goals in a global, highly dynamic and very competitive environment, it is absolutely necessary that a company keeps on enlarging its technological, systems and methodology envelope to minimize unit cost, reduce lead time and improve quality of products right at the product development stage. To accomplish these tasks, some innovative technologies, methodologies and systems have to be developed and integrated. For these things to happen, it is necessary that one understands the underlying phenomenon of product development. In this paper, the authors' objectives are to capture the product process interactions. They study the impact of various product design and process alternatives on cost, quality and lead time. For this purpose, they develop a simulation model which is coded in SIMAN. They illustrate the concepts using a case study of a journal bearing system.

articleTitle: A methodology for team effectiveness research
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: The use of teams of many types as an organizational strategy has dramatically increased and frequently these teams include engineers and other technical professionals. The increasing use of teams furthers the need for increasing collective understanding about team effectiveness. This paper presents a methodology for team-level research and results from a study to identify those team characteristics most related to effectiveness.

articleTitle: Measures of knowledge and their relevance to technology transfer
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
abstract: Summary form only as given. Technology transfer is defined as the transfer of knowledge, to include the "transformation" of knowledge into viable commodities that create value in the marketplace. Recently, learning, or knowledge acquisition was identified as possibly the sole source for sustainable competitive advantage in the market place. Researchers have generally failed to identify the key direct measures of knowledge in this context. Two case studies are used to suggest a framework to measure the knowledge.

articleTitle: Pathways for the improvement of indigenous technological innovation capability in China
publicationTitle: Innovation in Technology Management. The Key to Global Leadership. PICMET '97
